issues.claim: Senate amendment removed universal opt-out preference signal (UOOM/GPC) recognition requirement
issues.issue: A Senate amendment removed the requirement for controllers to recognize universal opt-out preference signals (e.g., GPC). This is a materially notable departure from Connecticut, Colorado, California, and recent state laws, and is not mentioned in the 'Unique Features' section.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a bullet noting that the enrolled bill does NOT require recognition of universal opt-out preference signals (GPC), unlike Connecticut, Colorado, California, and several recent state laws.

issues.claim: Report substantially overlaps with SCAN-20260412-001 on the same bill
issues.issue: SCAN-20260412-001 already covers Alabama HB 351 with the same key facts. Report 022 covers same provisions without clear differentiation. The unique value-add is the Compliance Action Items checklist and expanded exemption enumeration.
issues.suggested_fix: Reframe report explicitly as a compliance-playbook companion to SCAN-20260412-001 with a cross-reference in 'Related Reports'. Add introductory note: 'This report is a compliance companion to [link to 001]; for legislative background and analysis see that report.'

issues.claim: Alabama becoming the 21st state to 'enact' a comprehensive consumer privacy law
issues.issue: Inconsistent framing — some sections say 'enacted' while the Effective Date section correctly notes the Governor had not yet signed as of the report date.
issues.suggested_fix: Consistently describe status as 'passed by legislature, awaiting gubernatorial signature' throughout.
